transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln. Representative Douglas has brought formal charges that you voted in favor of the Sangamon County land grant while simultaneously representing the principal beneficiary of that grant in your law practice. The ethics of this chamber require that no member profit from legislation he has a hand in passing. You are well-regarded here, sir, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Well, Mr. Speaker, I thank you for the opportunity to address these accusations. I understand the gravity of the situation and wish to clarify my actions. Firstly, I must assert that I take my responsibilities as a legislator with utmost seriousness. 

In the case of the Sangamon County land grant vote, I did indeed support the measure. However, I must emphasize that my decision was based solely on what I believed to be in the best interest of the people I represent, and not influenced by any personal gain. 

As for the connection to my law practice, yes, it is true that I have a professional relationship with the beneficiary in question. However, I must stress that I have always made efforts to separate my legal work from my duties as a public servant. 

I hold myself to a high standard of ethics and integrity, and I assure you that I would never knowingly engage in any behavior that could be perceived as a conflict of interest. I am committed to upholding the trust that the people have placed in me, and I stand ready to address any further concerns or questions on this matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Mr. Lincoln, I appreciate your candor in acknowledging the facts of the matter. However, merely asserting that you "made efforts to separate" your legal work from your public duties does not fully address the substance of the charge. The issue, sir, is not just one of your personal intent, but of the perception and adherence to the ethical standards of this chamber.

You voted on a measure that directly benefited a client of your law practice. How, precisely, do you reconcile the professional fee you presumably received from this beneficiary with the principle that a legislator should not profit, directly or indirectly, from legislation he helps pass? It seems to many, myself included, that the benefit to your client, and by extension your firm, flows quite directly from the passage of that grant, a grant you yourself supported with your vote.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I understand the gravity of the situation, Mr. Speaker, and I appreciate your thorough examination of the matter. It is clear that the perception of impropriety is a serious concern that must be addressed with the utmost seriousness.

While I maintain that my intentions were always focused on serving the public good in my capacity as a legislator, I acknowledge the valid point you raise regarding the potential conflict of interest between my role as a lawmaker and my legal practice. It is essential for the public to have complete confidence in the integrity of their representatives, and any perception of self-interest or impropriety must be taken seriously.

In light of the concerns raised, I am prepared to take whatever steps are necessary to rectify this situation and to ensure that the ethical standards of this chamber are upheld without question. If it is deemed necessary to recuse myself from any future votes or discussions related to matters that could be perceived as conflicting with my professional interests, I am willing to do so in order to maintain the trust and confidence of my colleagues and constituents.

I am committed to transparency and accountability in all my actions, and I will work diligently to address any doubts or concerns that have been raised regarding my conduct in this matter. Thank you for your attention to this issue, and I am prepared to cooperate fully in any further inquiries or investigations that may be deemed necessary to resolve this issue in a manner consistent with the highest ethical standards of this honorable chamber.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

Your willingness to act ethically going forward is not a substitute for an accounting of the past.
